children: Saudi Arabia's latest $3.25 billion sukuk issuance is expected to support debt capital market growth through 2027, driven by funding diversification efforts and the financing needs of Vision 2030 projects.

The dual-tranche transaction, the kingdom's second international ijara sukuk issuance, attracted more than $16.5 billion in orders, highlighting the robustness of Saudi Arabia's debt capital market and investors' continued confidence in its credit profile despite a challenging regional backdrop.

“We expect the market to continue expanding through H2 2026 and 2027, underpinned by funding diversification initiatives, fiscal financing requirements, and the growing financing needs of the Kingdom's economic transformation agenda," Bashar Al-Natoor, MD, Global Head of Islamic Finance, Fitch Ratings, said.

The dominance of sukuk underscores its role as the primary funding instrument in the kingdom's debt market. Sukuk accounted for approximately 61% of Saudi Arabia's outstanding debt capital market at end of H1 2026.
“The market benefits from a broad issuer base, strong domestic demand and increasing international investor participation," Al-Natoor said.
While regional geopolitical tensions have tested market sentiment, Saudi issuers have maintained resilient credit fundamentals.

"Credit fundamentals in the Saudi sukuk market remain strong. More than 98% of Fitch-rated sukuk outstanding in Saudi Arabia are investment grade, with all rated issuers maintaining Stable Outlooks at end- H1 2026,” he added.

In May, the National Debt Management Center (NDMC) announced the completion of the 2026 Annual Borrowing Plan, having secured approximately 90% of the kingdom's funding needs prior to the geopolitical events in the region. NDMC said it will continue monitoring international markets for future funding opportunities.

"Recent issuance activity highlights the continued strength of the Saudi debt capital market. Sukuk issuance during July and August reached approximately $9.5 billion, supported by sovereign and financial institution transactions, demonstrating that issuers continue to access capital markets despite ongoing external uncertainties," Al-Natoor said.
(Reporting by Seban Scaria; editing by Daniel Luiz)

title: Saudi's $3.2bln sukuk sets stage for DCM expansion through 2027
